Analytic replay: test the immediate predecessor's cyclic displacement, then count subsets containing a fixed label using ordered gaps and multiply by n/s.
correctness.rationale: With s>0, consecutive clockwise gaps sum to n. A gap at most k violates independence, and any offending arc contains such a gap; for a singleton the only gap is n>k. Displacements up to 2k are available in at most two arcs, using one or two permitted positive increments. If a gap is at least 2k+2, the vertex 2k+1 after its start has no selected vertex in its preceding radius-2k interval. In this failure case 2k<n, so no modular representative of a walk can evade that test. Thus every gap must be in [k+1,2k+1], also when 2k>=n, where the upper condition is automatic. Marking one of the s selected vertices gives s times the number sought and is in bijection with a starting label and an ordered admissible gap vector; this works even for rotation-periodic subsets. Bounded composition inclusion-exclusion gives the stated count and can realize every sum from s(k+1) through s(2k+1). The allowed size interval is nonempty: putting f=floor(n/(k+1))>=1 gives n<=f(k+1)+k<=f(2k+1). For (9,2) the two admissible ordered gaps of length two are (4,5) and (5,4), giving nine sets; the only length-three vector is (3,3,3), giving three.
residual_risks: The recorded 90-case census is finite and auxiliary; the claim does not enumerate rotation orbits or general circulants.

evidence: The run-length recurrence applies to arbitrary internal lower and upper bounds and independently prescribed terminal upper bounds, so the two evaluations above require no extension of its theorem.
The quasi-kernel and distant domination papers give existence or size bounds, not the directed-circular-power enumerator. Those bounds are not the coverage basis.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger enumerative coverage is in a different vocabulary. Its constants can be specialized at every n,k,s, unlike the bounds in the nearby graph literature.

evidence: Subtracting the two trailing bounds leaves a one-block generating polynomial x^(k+1)+...+x^(2k+1), also the internal-block polynomial from the recurrence. Its s-fold product is the anchored count. Rotation invariance and counting the incidences with the selected label give a factor n/s. Consecutive support and the stated extrema follow from the support of this product.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This yields exactly the coefficient, positivity interval and both endpoints without new enumerative work. The unanchored count is not an orbit count, so stabilizers do not invalidate the incidence factor.

evidence: Put a one on every selected vertex. The two graph conditions are literally that between consecutive ones around the circle there are at least k and at most 2k zeros. Fixing the label 0 to be selected makes the encoded word begin with a one, with all its internal and trailing zero runs in [k,2k].

Kurmaev's linear first-one count A_n^nu(d,K,r) bounds the internal zero runs by [d,K] and the trailing run by [0,r]. The fixed-label count here is exactly A_n^s(k,2k,2k) minus A_n^s(k,2k,k-1), including s=1.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: No hypothesis relating circular to linear coding is assumed: cutting at the selected label makes precisely the final run the wraparound gap and subtraction imposes its lower bound.

value.rationale: The digraph family and its spectrum are natural, and the graph representation is useful exposition. But here the exact result reexpresses fixed-weight run-length enumeration via the nearest clockwise predecessor and an incidence normalization. The gap observation alone is the immediate translation of the two local conditions, with no separate nonroutine remainder or invariant established.
residual_risks: This verdict is about the delivered theorem as a distinct finding, not the utility of bounded-run methods in more general digraph problems.
